captions.instagram:
How does a chameleon change color?

A chameleon’s green is not paint. It is light bouncing off a lattice of crystals far smaller than a hair, and when a male gets excited the crystals spread apart and he turns orange. Slide the crystals and watch.

→ A chameleon grips with tong-like feet, a curling tail and eyes that swivel on their own.
→ The colour comes from tiny crystals: spaced close, they reflect blue, and yellow pigment makes it green.
→ Excited, the cells swell and the crystals spread out about 30%: the skin turns orange.
→ Rival males flash bright colours. The brighter, faster-changing male tends to win; the loser goes dark.
→ On a cool morning a chameleon goes dark to soak up more sunshine.

youtubeLong.description:
A chameleon’s green is not paint. It is light bouncing off a lattice of crystals far smaller than a hair, and when a male gets excited the crystals spread apart and he turns orange. Slide the crystals and watch.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/chameleonclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/chameleonclear

In this video:
• A skin built in layers. Under a chameleon’s clear outer skin sit yellow pigment cells, then two layers of crystal-filled iridophores, then dark melanophores with arms reaching up.
• Colour from crystals. Guanine crystals about 127 nm across sit in a neat lattice.
• Talking, not hiding. Chameleons do not copy their background.
• India’s chameleon. India has one chameleon, Chamaeleo zeylanicus, in scrub and dry forest across the peninsula.
• Chameleons and people. The Indian chameleon is in Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act after the 2022 amendment, so catching or trading one is a crime.
• How we found out. Aristotle thought chameleons changed colour by puffing up with air.
